 Massive recall on hot dogs, bacon, deli meat and more: USDA 
 by: Danielle Langenfeld 
 Posted: Oct 19, 2026 / 09:12 AM EDT 
 Updated: Oct 19, 2026 / 09:12 AM EDT 
 by: Danielle Langenfeld 
 Posted: Oct 19, 2026 / 09:12 AM EDT 
 Updated: Oct 19, 2026 / 09:12 AM EDT 
 SHARE 
 (WJW) — The U.S. Department of Agriculture has announced a massive meat recall on more than 1.5 million pounds of hot dogs, deli meat, bacon, bratwurst, and more.
 According to the nationwide recall alert , Kayem Foods Inc. is recalling about 1,584,361 pounds of its ready-to-eat (RTE) meat and poultry products because they may have been stored at improper temperatures.
 Skin care products tainted with mercury, warns FDA 
 The recall announced on Saturday, Oct. 17 by the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) said the problem was first flagged after the company received a complaint from a retail customer about warm product temperatures upon delivery on Oct. 1.
 “The establishment investigated and determined that they stored various RTE meat and poultry products in a warehouse cooler that experienced temperature deviations,” states the recall.
 The recall includes dozens of products sold under a variety of brand names. Recalled items include hot dogs, cocktail franks, kielbasa, and bratwurst, as well as deli meats such as ham, turkey, bologna, corned beef and liverwurst. The recall also includes a variety of flavored chicken sausage and meatballs. As well as bacon, brisket, ham steaks and more.
 According to FSIS, the items of concern were shipped to retail and food service locations nationwide and in Hong Kong. The items were produced approximately March 31, 2026, to Oct. 7, 2026. 
 Here’s what to look for:
 View product labels 
 List of products and UPC code numbers 
 Establishment numbers “EST. M/P 7839,” “EST. P 20935A” and “EST. M 9520” inside the USDA mark of inspection
 Local Circle K sells $15M scratch-off winner 
 So far, there have been no confirmed reports of sickness. However, anyone concerned about an illness is advised to contact a healthcare provider. 
 Consumers are advised to check their refrigerators and freezers. Anyone who purchased these products are urged not to consume them, instead throw the item away or return it to the place of purchase.
